messages:
Maya: FYI — ACME reported /v1/rerank returning strange score values (negatives and >1). They think scores should be probabilities. Posting sample response they sent.

Maya: request snippet they used:
```json
{
  "query": "best cables for headphones",
  "candidates": ["cable A", "cable B", "cable C"],
  "return_scores": true
}
```

Maya: response snippet:
```json
{
  "results": [
    {"candidate": "cable A", "score": -1.24},
    {"candidate": "cable B", "score": 0.37},
    {"candidate": "cable C", "score": 2.11}
  ]
}
```

Tom: thanks — do we know which model variant they called and whether they set any normalization flag? @Jenna any infra logs? :thinking:

Maya: they said model: rerank-open-1 (default), hosted region us-west, using our JS SDK (v1.4). No explicit normalize flag in their call.

Jenna: checked support-bot logs for thread id 8f4a — no HTTP 5xx, request succeeded. No transform was applied server-side. Scores are coming back as-is from the reranker model.

Tom: likely explanation: rerank endpoint returns raw scoring logits by default for greater flexibility. Those are not probabilities and can be negative or >1. If the client expects probabilities, they need to apply a softmax across the candidates.

Maya: can you paste a minimal repro (curl + python softmax) so I can send to customer?

Tom: sure — repro curl:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/rerank \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"query":"best cables for headphones","candidates":["A","B","C"],"return_scores":true}'
```

Tom: python softmax snippet to convert raw scores -> probs:
```python
import math
scores = [-1.24, 0.37, 2.11]
exp = [math.exp(s) for s in scores]
sum_exp = sum(exp)
probs = [e / sum_exp for e in exp]
print(probs)  # now sums to 1 and all in [0,1]
```

Jenna: note also edge-case: if client batches many queries into a single rerank call, make sure softmax is applied per-query group (per candidate set), not across the whole batch.

Maya: good point. ACME did send multiple queries inside one payload in earlier screenshot — I will clarify.

Tom: another helpful line: if they want us to return normalized probabilities for them, we can add a server-side option "normalize=true" in the SDK/endpoint (we don't enable by default due to perf and flexibility). Should we offer that as a short-term workaround?

Jenna: fine to offer as a support toggle for hosted customers, but we should file a tiny feature request so product tracks enabling it in SDKs.

Maya: I'll reply to the customer with: explanation (raw logits), repro (curl + softmax), and ask whether they want us to toggle server-side normalization. Also include warning about batching.

Maya: draft reply to ACME:
"Hi — thanks for the report. The rerank endpoint returns raw model scores (logits) by default, which are not probabilities and can be negative or greater than 1. To get probabilities, apply softmax across the candidate set. If you prefer, we can enable server-side normalization for your workspace temporarily. Also ensure you apply softmax per query, not across a batch of queries. Let us know which you prefer and we can enable the toggle or help patch your client." :thumbsup:

support-bot: noted ticket updated (T-4321). No service degradation.

Maya: sending now. Thanks all.
